sources.title: 3-D Anisotropic vs. Classical Incompressible Navier-Stokes Equations
sources.author: Ping Zhang
sources.version: Published proceedings chapter, online 13 July 2026, Volume 5, pp. 388-407
sources.license: CC BY 4.0, International Mathematical Union, verified in publisher metadata
sources.read: Publisher full-text HTML: sections 1-4 mathematical text and displayed theorems, including all of section 2, one-component criteria, special large data, MHD paragraph and analyticity statements; bibliography entries 1-71 and metadata. Energy identity (1.2) through scaling (1.3) was also independently expanded and read.
sources.not_read: No full visual PDF inspection; no blanket claim that cited research proofs were read.

sources.read: Section 1 including Definitions 1.1-1.3, Theorems 1.1-1.2, Corollary 1.1 and Remark 1.1; section 2 through Lemma 2.2 and Definition 2.4.
sources.checked: Hybrid high/low horizontal norm, anisotropic Bernstein dimensions, Chemin-Lerner order, direct proof of (2.1), small-unidirectional-derivative condition, and vertical-component high-horizontal heat remainder.
sources.not_read: Sections 3 onward proving the global theorem have not been read. The v1 vertical-component power is 4, whereas the SIAM report prints 8; these are distinct source formulations, not silently identical.

sources.read: Section 1; section 2 through Theorem 2.1 and (2.8); Lemma 3.1 statement and energy identity.
sources.checked: L^(3/2) initial vorticity, 4<p<6, fixed direction, horizontal Biot-Savart decomposition, H_theta definition, Fourier cone-splitting estimate (2.4), Propositions 2.1-2.3 and double-exponential bound. Independently derived the pressure sign using (-Delta)^(-1), instead of relying on an ambiguous Delta^(-1) convention.
sources.not_read: Full nonlinear estimates in sections 4-8 have not been read; they remain external inputs, not locally reproduced proofs.

sources.read: Introduction, Theorem 1.3, and section 2 through the rewritten equations and horizontal velocity decomposition (2.5).
sources.checked: Extension to 4<p<infinity adds initial vorticity in L2 to L^(3/2); p=infinity is not supplied by this argument.

sources.version: arXiv:2406.10865v2, 5 June 2025; version label retained despite a different generated HTML date
sources.read: HTML introduction through Theorem 1.3 and proof strategy; section 2 notation and Lemma 2.1; Lemma 2.3 statement (2.30) and complete proof. Actual v2 PDF pages 1-5 through the beginning of Theorem 1.3, plus PDF page 16 Lemma 2.3 statement and the start of its proof on page 18.
sources.checked: Subcritical Sobolev analyticity for gamma>1/2; uniform high-frequency tails; source-version dates. The actual PDF confirms the tail lemma is 2.3, although the introduction's cross-reference says 2.2.
sources.not_read: Full proof not read. The generated HTML is not evidence of a later arXiv version.

sources.read: Publisher metadata and abstract; all publicly exposed Appendix A text through the proof of Lemma A.2, including Bernstein, weighted Chemin-Lerner notation and Bony decompositions. Complete main theorem is read in SIAM Theorem 4.6, not in this research article.
sources.not_read: Paywalled main body and its precise base double-index Besov definition are inaccessible. Public appendix reading is not full research-article reading.

sources.read: Abstract and available introduction/Theorems 1.1-1.2 prose. Several mathematical formulas were not exposed by the preview.

sources.version: Retrieved page explicitly identifies arXiv:1812.00305v1, 2 December 2018
sources.read: Header/abstract and selected introduction through Definition 1.1 and all of Theorem 1.2, including A/B expressions.

source_level_checks.conclusion: NS has full Laplacian; ANS has Delta_h only, in R3, horizontal viscosity normalized to one and vertical viscosity zero. Hdot^(s,s') uses |xi_h|^(2s)|xi_3|^(2s'). B^(0,s) uses vertical dyadic blocks only with an l1 sum of L2 norms. Chemin-Lerner order is sum over blocks after taking time norms. The hybrid B4^(-1/2,1/2) includes both the high-horizontal mixed Lh4(Lv2) piece and the low-horizontal L2 piece; neither may be dropped.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.conclusion: Paicu gives local existence for arbitrary divergence-free B^(0,1/2) data, and global existence for small data. Theorem 2.3 requires ||u0h||_B4 exp(M||u03||_B4^4)<=c1: the smallness threshold depends on the vertical component. Theorem 2.4 adds L2 and vertical-derivative hypotheses and the full nested-exponential smallness condition. None solves unrestricted 3D large-data NS or ANS.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.conclusion: Continuous dependence holds locally in X_s for s>1/2 and a convergent sequence of data with a common lifespan. The nonuniform statement must be interpreted on balls/bounded families containing the constructed sequences, not literally every bounded subset, since every map on a singleton is uniformly continuous.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.conclusion: For initial vorticity in L^(3/2), the cited criterion uses fixed direction e and 4<p<6. Extension to 4<p<infinity in Theorem 3.6 requires initial vorticity in L^(3/2) intersection L2. Time-dependent direction is a separate cited result. The criterion is divergence of an integral when maximal lifespan is finite, not global existence for arbitrary data. H_theta=Hdot^(-1/2+theta,-theta), and the useful interval is 1/2-2/p<theta<1/6. The logarithmic endpoint theorem gives limsup>=c0, not divergence to infinity.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.topic: Special large data and spatial domain
source_level_checks.conclusion: Slow variation, small unidirectional derivative, high angular Fourier modes and cylinder results require their respective extra norms, constraints and domains. The cylinder is r<1 with Dirichlet boundary; its inequality |f|<=|f/r| cannot be moved to all R3. Theorem 3.10 has 0<=delta<1/4 and eta<1/2-delta. Delta=1 remains an open question in the survey.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.conclusion: Theorem 4.1 assumes an existing global NS solution and takes t to infinity. The refined instantaneous bounds take t to zero. Theorems 4.2-4.3 initially estimate v=u-e^(tDelta)u0, not directly u. Theorem 4.4 covers H^gamma, gamma>1/2, with a lower bound involving sqrt[t(|log t|+log|log t|)]. Theorem 4.5 is explicitly work in progress and reference 44 in preparation; it cannot be presented as established published research.
source_level_checks.status: Compared with all frozen local pages; see page_checks, source limitations and open findings.

source_level_checks.topic: ANS analytic data and horizontal smoothing
source_level_checks.conclusion: Global analytic ANS requires vertical analytic data, alpha,beta in (0,1) with alpha+beta>1, and the exact mixed smallness condition involving B^(0,1/2) and B^(-alpha,1/2-beta). For positive a<2sqrt(1-alpha), horizontal radius is at least a sqrt(t) and vertical radius retains delta0/2. The local result for arbitrary finite vertically analytic norm gives rh(t)/sqrt(t) tending to infinity as t down to zero; it does not give unrestricted global existence or creation of vertical analyticity from rough data.
source_level_checks.status: Published statement checked; local 4A1F imports only the band-limited short-time specialization, not the unresolved double-index global theorem.

source_discrepancies.observation: For s=1/2+epsilon, the printed product ||u0||_L2^epsilon ||u0||_Hdot^(0,s)^(1-epsilon) scales as lambda^(epsilon/2-epsilon^2), not as a critical norm for general epsilon.
source_discrepancies.independent_check: Under u_lambda(x)=lambda u(lambda x), L2 scales as lambda^(-1/2) and Hdot^(0,s) as lambda^(s-1/2). The critical interpolation product is ||u0||_L2^(1-1/(2s)) ||u0||_Hdot^(0,s)^(1/(2s)), equivalently the power product ||u0||_L2^(2s-1)||u0||_Hdot^(0,s).
source_discrepancies.required_action: Do not copy the printed exponents while calling them scaling invariant; verify the original theorem if importing this statement.

source_discrepancies.observation: The literal claim of nonuniform continuity on any bounded subset is false on finite subsets and compact subsets.
source_discrepancies.required_action: Use the precise bounded-sequence conclusion or a justified bounded-ball formulation.

source_discrepancies.observation: The displayed weight contains sqrt(t ln|t|), which is not real for small positive t.
source_discrepancies.required_action: Use sqrt(t|ln t|), consistently with (4.4), and take 0<t<=t1.

source_discrepancies.observation: The displayed B is a positive Duhamel integral whereas NS written as u_t-Delta u=-P div(u tensor u) requires a minus sign.
source_discrepancies.required_action: If defining B, make the Duhamel convention explicit and consistent with the momentum equation.

source_discrepancies.observation: The displayed vector (0,u0,hh) is dimensionally ambiguous because (2.7) defines u0,hh as a three-component vector.
source_discrepancies.required_action: Original LPZ-v1 Theorem 1.2 confirms the vector is (0,u0,hh^3). Use the vertical component.

source_discrepancies.location: Published Theorem 2.4 versus LPZ-v1 Theorem 1.2 and Corollary 1.1
source_discrepancies.observation: The report prints a vertical-component eighth power in the outer exponential, while the checked original v1 has fourth power.
source_discrepancies.required_action: Bind any quoted smallness condition to its actual source version, with the nested exponential and A_N definition intact. The stronger-looking report formulation is not automatically algebraically equivalent.

source_discrepancies.observation: The introduction refers to the uniform high-frequency-tail result as Lemma 2.2. Both actual PDF and HTML place that statement at Lemma 2.3, equation (2.30); Lemma 2.2 is a weighted Duhamel estimate.
source_discrepancies.required_action: Point the local tail lemma to Lemma 2.3. A compactness proof for a continuous H^gamma-valued path is a legitimate independent local proof and should be identified as such.

snapshot_status: Accepted final frozen snapshot after full first-pass reading, full rereading of all changed pages, full reading of new 4A28, and final rereading of the integer-mode correction in 4A25. Every tree digest agrees with the packet.

structural_checks.method: Independent read-only ID/title/body-link/hash checks and DFS against the shared prerequisite registry merged with this packet.
structural_checks.limits: Structural closure is not a new mathematical rereview of all 217 pre-existing nodes. All 23 current direct reused pages were read. No build/render/release validation was performed.

page_checks.checks: Equation distinction, full versus directional dissipation, one-component criteria and short-time analytic conclusions remain separate; overview does not claim unrestricted global regularity.
Delta_h acts only in two horizontal directions; viscosity normalization and R3/divergence-free hypotheses checked against report (1.1)/(2.1).
Transport and pressure cancellation, horizontal-only gradient square and integrated factor 2 checked; decay and smoothness retained.

Fourier normalization (2pi)^-3, anisotropic weights, homogeneous completion/low-frequency representative convention, inhomogeneous H^(0,s), vector norms checked. Existing Schwartz-to-seminorm chain is sufficient.
Dyadic horizontal/vertical cutoffs, telescoping partition, support annuli and homogeneous low modes checked.
Vertical l1 sum of L2 blocks, critical exponent 1/2 and homogeneous convention checked; not a double-index norm.
Chemin-Lerner order is block sum after time norm; it is not silently exchanged with the ordinary Bochner norm.
NS scaling changes L2 by lambda^-1/2, anisotropic H by lambda^(s+sigma-1/2); critical indices checked.
Low/high vertical block split and optimizing dyadic threshold give A^1/2 B^1/2; A=0 or B=0 cases retained.
Horizontal dyadic heat decay and k>=ell frequency comparison verified by Plancherel; no vertical smoothing claimed off that cone.
Frequency-modulated tensor product gives (N-1)^s lower bound and N-independent input norm. Direct Plancherel link to 0W01 and packet dependency verified (PZ-F4 resolved).
Both high-horizontal Lh4(Lv2) square-sum and low-horizontal L2 term retained in the hybrid X4 norm; compared to LPZ-v1.
Local arbitrary-data and small-data global ANS conclusions are distinct; B^(0,1/2), divergence-free data and time regularity checked.
Differentiating exponential time weight yields the extra nonnegative damping with correct sign; does not itself prove a nonlinear estimate.
Small horizontal norm times exp(M vertical norm^4) retained; vertical component not required small, but threshold depends on it.
All L2/derivative/hybrid norm assumptions, nested exponential and third-component high-horizontal heat remainder compared with LPZ-v1; source's fourth power is explicitly version-bound.
div_h uh=-partial3 u3 follows from divergence-free condition; identifies stretching but gives no standalone a priori bound.
Horizontal div/curl inversion and signs checked; inverse horizontal Laplacian requires the stated low-frequency convention.
Curl, vertical stretching, pressure recovery and signs using (-Delta)^-1 checked; nonlinear horizontal decomposition uses 4A11.
H_theta weights and horizontal/vertical frequency-cone split checked; theta range is not extrapolated beyond admissible interval.
Lp coefficient 4(p-1)/p^2 and p=3/2 coefficient 8/9 verified; p<2 regularized testing retained. Stokes and expanding-ball boundary limit now explicit (PZ-F5 resolved).
Fujita-Kato homogeneous half-derivative strong solution framework and small-data versus arbitrary-data lifespan distinction checked.
Fixed direction, omega0 in L^(3/2), 4<p<6 and finite-time integral blow-up checked. Wider finite-p range adds omega0 in L2; p=infinity not asserted.
Both nested-exponential factors and exponents checked against CZ-v1 Proposition 2.3, not inferred from the report's abbreviated narrative.
Horizontal logarithmic weight and the half-order Sobolev integrand checked; logarithm regularization avoids low-frequency singularity.
Endpoint conclusion is limsup >= c0, not infinity; fixed-component interpretation and initial regularity retained.
Horizontal gradient cubic-term cancellation checked algebraically with divergence-free substitution; no unsupported sign-definiteness claimed.
Exponential Fourier weight gives holomorphic extension on every smaller tube by integrable inverse transform; horizontal-only weight cannot create vertical radius.
r rho-t rho^2 <= r^2/(4t), Plancherel and directional variant checked.
Continuity plus uniform smallness near zero gives high-frequency tail convergence. Exact source is now LZ-v2 Lemma 2.3 (2.30), PDF p16; independent proof retained (PZ-F1 resolved).
gamma>1/2, eta threshold 0.01 t^-1/2, min defining beta and coefficient 3 beta checked against LZ-v2 Theorem 1.2. All conclusions are short-time and do not extend lifespan.
Only band-limited data/short-time horizontal analyticity imported. No claim of global ANS from unrestricted analytic data; ambiguous general double-Besov statement deliberately not imported.
Bony low-high/high-low/comparable-frequency grouping and low-frequency convention checked; finite identity is not represented as an unconditional product theorem for arbitrary distributions.
s>1/2, convergent initial sequence, common lifespan and continuity topology checked; no uniform-continuity upgrade.
Bounded sequence separation is the correct nonuniform-continuity witness. Literal any bounded subset would fail on singletons and is not repeated.
Oscillatory vector field remains divergence-free; frequency localization N>4R sufficient; X4 estimate and large-energy contrast checked.
Vertical dilation gives epsilon^-1/2 L2 size and epsilon^1/2 vertical derivative size, preserving the stated field constraints.

Nonzero integer angular frequency now explicit, ensuring a single-valued 2pi-periodic scalar field. Scalar angular energy, volume factor, bounded-radius lower bound and full-space limitation checked. Generic coordinates correctly target 4A28 (PZ-F3 and PZ-F6 resolved).
M norm, N^-1 angular component and divergence constraints rechecked using the new correct general frame definition. Cited full-space global theorem remains external (PZ-F3 resolved).
Full A, mathfrak A, B and data conditions checked against SIAM Theorem 3.8. Body example link retained but removed from actual prerequisites (PZ-F2 resolved).

r>0 and angle modulo 2pi; e_r,e_theta,e_z orthonormal basis; angular derivatives; distinction between physical coefficient u_theta and coordinate basis r e_theta; chain-rule differential operators and all four divergence terms checked explicitly. Axis smoothness is correctly formulated in Cartesian components. One reusable coordinate question, not a special-axisymmetry theorem.
Published title/DOI/pages/license, supplementary version identities and read-versus-cited-proof boundaries checked.

resolved_findings.title: Correct the high-frequency-tail source locator
resolved_findings.detail: The actual LZ-v2 PDF has uniform high-frequency smallness at Lemma 2.3, (2.30), PDF page 16, with proof on pages 18-19. Lemma 2.2 is a different weighted Duhamel estimate. The introduction itself has the stale 2.2 cross-reference. The local short-time argument is mathematically valid.

resolved_findings.title: Do not register the slow-variation example as a prerequisite of the global theorem

The large-N theorem instead concerns non-axisymmetric data with nonzero angular velocity. 4A25 already supplies the scalar coordinate map, but 4A26 never spells out the angular basis used by its component formulas.

Update prerequisite records consistently.
